headline: Efficiency gets more output from less input—often the cheapest and cleanest energy is what you don't use
universal_truth: Reduction often beats production; not needing something is better than having more of it
fun_facts: LED lights use 75% less energy than incandescent bulbs for the same light output
Better insulation can cut heating costs by 50%—without generating any new energy
The US economy produces twice the GDP per unit of energy compared to 1970
discussion_questions: Where could you get more output from the same input—or same output from less?
What are you wasting that efficiency could recover?
When is reducing demand better than increasing supply?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: The cheapest kilowatt is the one you don't use. Efficiency gets you the same result with less input—same light from less electricity, same comfort from less heating. Before producing more, ask: could you need less?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: We often focus on production—make more, get more. But efficiency is equally powerful. Why is reduction undervalued?

options.text: Production is visible, reduction is invisible—we celebrate new things more than optimized things; but not needing something is often better than having more of it
options.response: Yes. Building a power plant is dramatic. Insulating buildings is boring. But they can achieve the same result—and efficiency is often cheaper, cleaner, and faster. Invisible solutions are still solutions.
It does, but we're usually far from those limits—significant gains remain available...

q1.title: Same Output, Less Input
q1.script: Efficiency isn't sacrifice—it's optimization. LED lights aren't dimmer; they're smarter. Efficient cars aren't slower; they're better designed. More from less, not less from less.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Same Output, Less Input"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Cheapest and Cleanest
q2.script: Energy you don't use has no cost, no pollution, no infrastructure needs. Efficiency is often the fastest, cheapest, cleanest solution. But it's invisible, so it gets less attention.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Personal Efficiency
q3.script: You can be more efficient too—in time, money, energy. Before asking 'how do I get more?', ask 'how do I need less?' Reducing demand often beats increasing supply.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Reduction often beats production. Not needing something is better than having more of it. Consider efficiency before expansion.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 278. Tomorrow, we'll explore making less trash—waste reduction. Until then, find one area where efficiency could help.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Efficiency Scan - Where Can You Need Less?
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify efficiency opportunities before seeking more
growTrack.activity: Where are you inefficient—wasting time, money, energy, attention? Before seeking more resources, could you use existing resources better? Efficiency gains are often easier, cheaper, and faster than acquiring more.
